newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Blockbuster Video aims to open 300 Taiwan shops.
newsitem.headline: Blockbuster Video aims to open 300 Taiwan shops.

text.p: Blockbuster Video International, a unit of U.S. media giant Viacom Inc, charges into the Taiwan market on Friday -- opening the first of a planned 300 video rental stores on the island.
"Our target is to open 300 Blockbuster video stores in three years," Taiwan branch marketing director Adonis Chang told Reuters by telephone.
Chang declined to say how much the company was investing.
Blockbuster acknowledged it was entering a crowded market, but expects to capture the market with higher quality and better service.
"Those existing video stores are usually smaller ones, so we are better positioned due to our high-quality tapes and wider selection," Chang said.

Taiwan already has about 1,700 video stores -- mostly small family-run shops with spotty collections. The market is huge as Taiwanese spend an estimated T$3 billion (US$109 million) on video rentals per year.
Blockbuster expects to have 100,000 regular clients in the first year of operation, Chang said.
The video giant said 70 percent of Taiwan's families owned video cassette recorders.

Chang said Blockbuster was not worried by competition from the half-dozen movie channels available on cable television, saying it would maintain market share by marketing movies on video about one year before they appear on cable.
"Cable is no threat to us, as our movies will be available earlier," he said.
Chang said Taiwan would be Blockbuster's home base for pushes into Hong Kong and China over the next three years.
"China's rate of VCR ownership is still low, but its economy is booming," he said.
Blockbuster said it has more than 5,000 stores around the world with over 60 million members.
Chang said Blockbuster could help cut down on video piracy because Taiwan's increasingly affluent viewers prefer the high quality of legitimate rentals.
"All our tapes are best quality and people will prefer that," he said.
